findings.name: authenticated_security_definer_function_executable
findings.title: Signed-In Users Can Execute SECURITY DEFINER Function
findings.description: Detects `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that are callable by signed-in users. Revoke `EXECUTE`, switch the function to `SECURITY INVOKER`, or move it out of your exposed API schema if signed-in users should not call it.
findings.detail: Function `public.parent_maya_note_sessions(p_calls uuid[])` can be executed by the `authenticated` role as a `SECURITY DEFINER` function via `/rest/v1/rpc/parent_maya_note_sessions`. Revoke `EXECUTE` or switch it to `SECURITY INVOKER` if that is not intentional.

assessment: Expected authenticated SECURITY DEFINER reader. The function returns only safe metadata for the auth.uid owner of an ended session with a saved note. Search path is empty. Hosted positive and negative ownership controls passed. Parent access to maya_calls remains denied.
